title: A better general social network
summary: A new social network that is more private, more positive, or less ad-driven than the incumbents.
keywords: social network, feed, friends, privacy, ad-free, followers, posts, alternative
whyTempting: Lots of people say they dislike the social networks they use every day. That frustration looks like pent-up demand for an alternative, and launches often get a burst of sign-ups and press.
whyItFails:
People stay on networks because their friends are there, not because they like the product. A new network has to move whole social graphs at once, and a sign-up spike is not the same as people posting week after week.

Even companies with enormous resources and existing users have failed at this, which suggests money and distribution aren't the missing ingredient.
whatWouldChange:
A new network needs a specific community that is badly served today and will move together, rather than 'everyone'.

It also needs a format or behaviour that is genuinely new, the way photo sharing, short video or disappearing messages were, rather than a better-run version of an existing feed.

attempts.notes: A private network limited to close friends.
Launched by Google with huge distribution, but failed to become a daily habit.
Went viral at launch, then usage dropped off.

reasons.detail: Value depends on friends already being there, so early users find it empty.
Network effects keep people on existing platforms even when they complain.
Launch-day curiosity didn't turn into regular posting.
Growth brings spam and abuse that must be handled from day one.
